# `aitbc system env-set`

Set KEY=VALUE pairs in a service's env file under /etc/aitbc, then restart it. The env file is resolved from the unit's ``EnvironmentFile`` declaration (falling back to ``/etc/aitbc/<unit>.env``). Values are never echoed — only key names are reported.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc system env-set [OPTIONS] SERVICE [ASSIGNMENTS...]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | text | yes | — |
| `assignments` | text … | no | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--env-file` | text | — | no | Env file to edit (default: the unit's EnvironmentFile) |
| `--no-restart` | flag | `false` | no | Write the env file without restarting the service |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc system env-set SERVICE
```
